item.title: Prentiss County unemployment rises to 3.7% in October
item.description: Prentiss County, Mississippi, including Booneville. The October 2026 preliminary residence-based estimates in the Mississippi Department of Employment Security report put the local unemployment rate at 3.7% in October after a revised 3.2% in September. The August rate was 3.1%. The department counts 9,823 county residents in the October civilian labor force. Of them 9,459 were employed and 364 were unemployed. In September the labor force numbered 9,918, with 9,602 employed and 316 unemployed. The unemployed total rose by 48 residents. The employed count fell by 143. The change in the civilian labor force was -95 people. The survey describes people age 16 and older by where they live. A resident who commutes outside the county remains part of the county residence-based estimates. These counts should not be described as employers adding or eliminating positions. The number unemployed and the number employed together equal the civilian labor force in each month. The comparable Mississippi rate was 3.6%, based on 45,914 unemployed and 1,214,626 employed residents in a civilian labor force of 1,260,540. Both state and county figures in this comparison are unadjusted for seasonal changes. A separate county table in the same release lists 27 initial unemployment insurance claims and 119 continued claims in October compared with 16 initial and 123 continued claims in September. Insurance claims are an administrative measure. They should not be added together or treated as the number of unemployed residents. September is revised and October is preliminary. The tables do not establish what caused any change. The department’s county series gives these monthly rates earlier in 2026: June at 3.9%, July at 3.7%, August at 3.1%, September at 3.2%, October at 3.7%. Source documents: https://mdes.ms.gov/media/23357/labormarketdata.pdf (labor force estimates and county unemployment insurance claims); https://mdes.ms.gov/media/8735/urate.pdf (county monthly unemployment series); https://mdes.ms.gov/media/8654/uratesmapbw.pdf (October county unemployment rate map).

item.title: Booneville forecast puts heaviest Thanksgiving travel rain Wednesday, with a low of 26 Thursday night
item.description: The National Weather Service Memphis forecast office issued its Monday evening area forecast discussion at 5:50 p.m. Central November 23, 2026. The following local forecast is for the city of Booneville, Prentiss County, Mississippi. The NWS point service identifies the grid as MEG 97,47 at the center of Booneville. These are forecast conditions in Central time, not observations. For travelers leaving before Thanksgiving, Tuesday afternoon is the drier window in the Booneville point forecast. Rain becomes likely after midnight Tuesday night, with the highest probabilities on Wednesday. The Wednesday daytime local forecast calls for three quarters of an inch to one inch of rain. The Wednesday night local forecast calls for an additional one quarter to one half inch. Rainfall totals are possible amounts for those separate forecast periods, not guaranteed totals. The hourly forecast pinpoints the overnight change for drivers. Tuesday, November 24 at 6 PM Central in Booneville: 50 degrees Fahrenheit and a 1 percent chance of precipitation. Tuesday, November 24 at 10 PM Central in Booneville: 45 degrees Fahrenheit and a 2 percent chance of precipitation. Wednesday, November 25 at 2 AM Central in Booneville: 44 degrees Fahrenheit and a 38 percent chance of precipitation. Wednesday, November 25 at 6 AM Central in Booneville: 44 degrees Fahrenheit and a 94 percent chance of precipitation. Tuesday, 2026-11-24: Mostly sunny. High near 56, with temperatures falling to around 52 in the afternoon. North northeast wind 10 to 15 mph. Tuesday Night, 2026-11-24: Rain likely after midnight. Mostly cloudy, with a low around 41. North northeast wind 5 to 10 mph. Chance of precipitation is 60%. New rainfall amounts less than a tenth of an inch possible. Wednesday, 2026-11-25: Rain. Cloudy. High near 53, with temperatures falling to around 49 in the afternoon. North northeast wind 5 to 10 mph. Chance of precipitation is 100%. New rainfall amounts between three quarters and one inch possible. Wednesday Night, 2026-11-25: Rain likely. Mostly cloudy, with a low around 36. North northwest wind 5 to 10 mph. Chance of precipitation is 70%. New rainfall amounts between a quarter and half of an inch possible. Thanksgiving Day, 2026-11-26: Partly sunny. High near 48, with temperatures falling to around 44 in the afternoon. West northwest wind around 15 mph. Thursday Night, 2026-11-26: A slight chance of rain showers before midnight. Mostly clear, with a low around 26. West wind 5 to 15 mph. Chance of precipitation is 20%. Friday, 2026-11-27: Sunny, with a high near 55. West wind 5 to 10 mph. Friday Night, 2026-11-27: Mostly clear, with a low around 29. The area discussion describes a slow-moving system bringing rain east of Memphis Wednesday. Its broader outlook says rain may linger on Thanksgiving mainly along and north of Interstate 40. Use the Booneville point forecast for local conditions. Local forecast and public updates: https://forecast.weather.gov/MapClick.php?lat=34.6581&lon=-88.5667 . Period forecast: https://api.weather.gov/gridpoints/MEG/97,47/forecast . item.title: Booneville High, New Site, Wheeler and the Prentiss County career center appear on TVA’s STEM award roster
item.description: Booneville High School — Prentiss County Electric Power Association. New Site High School — Prentiss County Electric Power Association. Prentiss County Career and Technology Center — Prentiss County Electric Power Association. Wheeler Attendance Center — Prentiss County Electric Power Association. TVA's spreadsheet lists four entries under Prentiss County Electric Power Association. They represent two public school districts. The Booneville School District school directory identifies Booneville High School. The Prentiss County School District separately identifies New Site High School, Wheeler Attendance Center and the district's career and technical center. The career center gives its Booneville address as 302 W. George E. Allen Drive. Its regular course offerings include computer science and engineering, welding, construction and carpentry, auto service technology, and agriculture and natural resources. The course list describes the center. The award spreadsheet has three columns, district, power company and school, with no project descriptions or amounts for individual recipients. The four entries therefore establish the identity of each recipient. No particular course, project or expenditure can be attributed to these awards from those records. The Tennessee Valley Authority and Bicentennial Volunteers, Inc., its retiree organization, announced the regional awards on November 23, 2026. The 2026–27 list contains 334 school entries across the region, 36 in TVA's Mississippi district. The program awards $1.5 million regionwide and TVA estimates about 96,000 students will benefit across the region. The $5,000 figure is an upper limit for an individual award. It is not the amount awarded to a named school. Eligible schools receive electricity through a local power company served by TVA. The competitive process gives preference to proposals dealing with the environment, energy, economic development or solving community problems. The Tennessee STEM Innovation Network is a program partner and Battelle manages the network. TVA says that since 2018 the partners have provided more than $10.5 million through these awards, supporting more than 940,000 students across the region. Primary award announcement: https://www.tva.com/the-powerhouse/stories/tva-awards--1.5-million-to-support-stem-education-across-the-valley_edu Award program and full recipient list: https://www.tva.com/learn/stem-awards Official workbook: https://tva-azr-eastus-cdn-ep-tvawcm-prd.azureedge.net/cdn-tvawcma/docs/default-source/tva-stem/2026--2027-tva-stem-award.xlsx?sfvrsn=87e985be_1 School district sources: https://www.boonevilleschools.org/, https://www.prentisscountyschools.com/, https://www.prentisscountyctc.com/ TVA's previous recipient list confirms that the Prentiss County Career and Technology Center also received a STEM award in 2024–25. The earlier Mississippi list also includes Hills Chapel. That is historical context; Hills Chapel is not among the four current entries under the Prentiss County Electric Power Association. The county district's school directory shows how the current recipients differ in the grades they serve. New Site High School serves grades nine through twelve at 1020 Highway 4 East in New Site. Wheeler Attendance Center serves prekindergarten through twelfth grade at 318 County Road 5011 and has a Booneville mailing address. The district lists the career center separately. Previous TVA list: https://www.tva.com/stem/2024-2025-grant-recipients . District directory: https://www.prentisscountyschools.com/our-district/our-schools .
